## How the unit tests are run

The unit tests live under `tests/unit/`. Looking at `package.json`, the script that runs them is:

```json
"test:unit": "node --test --experimental-strip-types \"tests/unit/**/*.test.ts\""
```

So the command is:

```
pnpm test:unit
```

(equivalently `npm run test:unit`). No test framework dependency is involved — the project intentionally runs on **Node's built-in `node:test`** together with Node's native TypeScript type-stripping (`--experimental-strip-types`, valid for Node ≥ 22.6), which is consistent with the project's zero-runtime-dependency policy (ADR-0009). ## What I added

One new test case in `tests/unit/util.test.ts`, inside the existing `text` describe block. It covers a genuine edge case in the `sliceLines` utility from `src/util/text.ts`:

- **The case:** calling `sliceLines` with an `offsetLine` that is past the end of the document (e.g. `sliceLines('l1\nl2\nl3', 5)`).
- **Why it's genuine:** an offset can overshoot when a window was computed against stale content — the file shrank between when it was read and when the slice was requested. This is exactly the kind of boundary a future refactor could break.
